chunks.title: Decreased vision: sort it in 3 questions
chunks.tldr: Ask: one eye or both? sudden or slow? painful or painless? Sudden painless one-eye loss = vascular (CRAO/CRVO, AION, GCA), vitreous haemorrhage, RD. Sudden painful = cornea, uveitis, acute angle closure, endophthalmitis, optic neuritis.
points: Monocular transient (<24 h) painless: amaurosis fugax, disc drusen, impending CRVO, ocular ischaemia, orthostatic hypotension.
Transient painful: migraine, dry eye, SPK.
Binocular sudden painless: stroke (homonymous hemianopia), vertebrobasilar insufficiency, papilloedema.
Binocular painful: migraine, pituitary apoplexy, papilloedema with headache.
Chronic painless: refractive error, cataract, glaucoma, corneal scar, optic neuropathy, AMD/diabetic retinopathy.
Optic neuritis: pain on eye movement but ~10% painless.
After trauma: cornea, hyphaema, rupture, cataract, commotio, RD, VH, lens dislocation, traumatic optic neuropathy.
Diagnosis of exclusion: nonphysiologic loss.

head: Painless
Painful
rows: Ulcer, uveitis, AACG, endophthalmitis, optic neuritis

chunks.hook: 1 eye vs 2, fast vs slow, ouch vs no-ouch — 3 questions narrow it to a short list.

cards.q: Sudden painless monocular vision loss — four big causes?
cards.a: Retinal artery/vein occlusion, ischaemic optic neuropathy/GCA, vitreous haemorrhage, retinal detachment.

cards.q: Sudden bilateral vision loss with headache and ophthalmoplegia?

chunks.title: Distortion, diplopia & oscillopsia
chunks.tldr: Monocular diplopia (persists covering the other eye) = optics: refraction, cornea (keratoconus), cataract, iris holes, dry eye. Binocular diplopia (goes when either eye covered) = misalignment: intermittent → myasthenia/phoria; constant → III/IV/VI palsy, orbit (thyroid, fracture), INO.
points: Distortion: refractive error/astigmatism (lid mass, chalazion), macular disease (CSR, oedema, AMD), irregular cornea, intoxication.
Rarer distortion: ectasia, drops (miotics/cycloplegics), RD, migraine, hypotony.
Monocular diplopia less common: dislocated lens/IOL, macular disease, nonphysiologic.
Binocular after surgery: residual anaesthesia, slipped muscle, scleral buckle, aniseikonia.
Oscillopsia ('jumping'): acquired nystagmus, INO, myasthenia, vestibular loss, opsoclonus, superior oblique myokymia.
chunks.hook: Cover one eye: still double = the eye's optics. Gone = the eyes' alignment.

cards.q: Diplopia persists when the good eye is covered — where is the problem?
cards.a: In the eye itself (refractive, corneal, lens, iris) – monocular diplopia.

cards.q: Intermittent binocular diplopia worse later in the day?

chunks.title: Flashes, floaters, glare & halos
chunks.tldr: Flashes: PVD, retinal break/RD, migraine. Floaters/spots: vitreous syneresis, PVD, vitreous haemorrhage, uveitis. Halos: cataract, corneal oedema (acute angle closure), Fuchs, digoxin/chloroquine. Formed hallucinations in poor vision = Charles Bonnet.
points: Less common flashes: white dot syndromes, occipital lesions, VBI, optic neuropathy, IOL dysphotopsia.
Transient spots = migraine.
Some patients' 'spot' is really a scotoma (retina, nerve, brain).
Glare: cataract, PCO, corneal oedema, dilated pupil, post-refractive surgery.
Halos also: pigment dispersion, contact lens overwear, post-refractive surgery.

cards.q: Elderly patient with poor vision seeing formed images, insight intact?
Coloured halos around lights with a red painful eye?
cards.a: Corneal oedema from acute angle-closure glaucoma.

chunks.title: Lid symptoms: swelling, crusting, twitch, can't close
chunks.tldr: Swollen + red + tender: hordeolum, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, preseptal/orbital cellulitis, trauma, contact dermatitis, HSV/VZV. Swollen, not inflamed: chalazion, fat prolapse, mass, heart/kidney/thyroid disease, SVC syndrome. Twitch: usually myokymia (caffeine, stress).
points: Crusting: blepharitis, meibomitis, conjunctivitis; less often canaliculitis, NLDO, dacryocystitis.
Lash loss: trauma, burn, sebaceous carcinoma, infection, alopecia, trichotillomania.
Twitch others: blepharospasm (both sides), hemifacial spasm, Tourette, trigeminal neuralgia.
Lagophthalmos: proptosis, lid laxity/ectropion, scarring, VII palsy, botox, cosmetic surgery, thyroid eye disease.
chunks.hook: Lash loss + thick lid in an older person = rule out sebaceous carcinoma.

cards.q: Non-inflamed bilateral lid swelling — systemic causes?
cards.a: Cardiac, renal or thyroid disease; superior vena cava syndrome.

chunks.title: Red eye: work from outside in
chunks.tldr: Check layer by layer: lids (trichiasis, entropion, blepharitis, floppy lid), conjunctiva (conjunctivitis, subconj haemorrhage, pinguecula, SLK), cornea (keratitis, CL problems, FB, erosion, burns), deeper (uveitis, scleritis, endophthalmitis, angle closure, c-c fistula).
points: Adnexa also: lagophthalmos, rosacea, dacryocystitis, canaliculitis.
Conjunctiva also: ophthalmia neonatorum, GPC, symblepharon (pemphigoid, SJS), neoplasia.
Cornea also: neurotrophic keratopathy, medicamentosa, pterygium.
Other: prostaglandin drops, cluster headache, corkscrew vessels = carotid–cavernous fistula.
Red flags: pain, photophobia, reduced vision, abnormal pupil, high IOP.
chunks.hook: Lids → conj → cornea → inside; worry if it hurts, blurs, or the pupil is odd.

cards.q: Red eye with corkscrew conjunctival vessels?

chunks.title: Itch, burn, FB feeling, tearing & photophobia
chunks.tldr: Itch = allergy until proven otherwise (also blepharitis, dry eye, GPC). Burning = blepharitis/dry eye. FB sensation: dry eye, trichiasis, FB, erosion, loose suture. Tearing: painful → cornea/uveitis/trichiasis; painless → dry eye (reflex), NLDO, ectropion. Kids tearing → NLDO or congenital glaucoma.
points: Burning less common: inflamed pterygium, episcleritis, SLK, toxicity from drops/makeup/CL solution.
Crocodile tears: aberrant VII regeneration.
Photophobia with abnormal eye: corneal problem, anterior uveitis; also albinism, aniridia, dilated pupil, congenital glaucoma.
Photophobia with normal eye: migraine, meningitis, SAH, concussion, retrobulbar neuritis, trigeminal neuralgia.
Night blindness: undercorrected myopia, advanced glaucoma, miosis, RP, CSNB, PRP, drugs; rarer vit A deficiency, gyrate atrophy, choroideremia.
chunks.hook: Photophobia + normal eye → think brain (migraine, meningitis, bleed).

cards.q: Watery, light-sensitive infant with big cloudy cornea?
Photophobia with a completely normal eye exam — serious causes?
cards.a: Meningitis, subarachnoid haemorrhage (also migraine, retrobulbar neuritis).

chunks.title: Eye pain by location
chunks.tldr: Ocular mild: dry eye, blepharitis, conjunctivitis, episcleritis, FB. Ocular severe: corneal ulcer/abrasion, chemical/UV burn, anterior uveitis, scleritis, endophthalmitis, acute angle closure. Orbital: cellulitis, inflammation, tumour, optic neuritis, microvascular nerve palsy. Periorbital: GCA, trigeminal neuralgia, referred dental/sinus.
points: Mild also: SPK, SLK, drop toxicity, CL problem, ocular ischaemic syndrome, asthenopia.
Orbital also: dacryoadenitis, migraine/cluster, postherpetic neuralgia.
Asthenopia (eye strain): uncorrected refraction, phoria, convergence insufficiency, accommodative spasm.
chunks.hook: Scleritis pain wakes you up; episcleritis just annoys.

cards.q: Severe ocular pain that can be from inside the eye — four causes?
cards.a: Anterior uveitis, scleritis, endophthalmitis, acute angle-closure glaucoma.
